newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Braidwood, Ill., nuke boosting power.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Braidwood, Ill., nuke boosting power.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's (ComEd) 1,120 megawatt (MW) Braidwood nuclear unit 1 was boosting power Monday after a weekend outage for repairs, a company spokesman said.
"It will take a couple of days to reach full power," spokesman Gary Wald said Monday, adding the unit was currently producing at about 30 percent of capacity.
Braidwood 1, located in Braidwood, Ill., was taken off line early Saturday for valve repairs, Wald said.
Other ComEd Illinois nuclear units were also expected to boost power following repairs.
The 789 MW Quad Cities unit 1, located in Cordova, Ill., was expected to operate at about 29 percent of capacity until a level control valve on a moisture separator reheater tank could be repaired.
Wald could not estimate how long the Quad Cities repair might take.
Also, ComEd's 794 MW Dresden unit 2 at Morris, Ill., was expected to operate at near 80 percent of capacity until repairs could be completed on a control rod drive, Wald said.
He could not estimate when the unit would begin ramping up to full power.

ComEd's 794 MW Dresden unit 3 was expected to begin startup next week, returning from an outage which began June 30 when the unit was shut for inspection and a fire protection system upgrade, Wald said.
ComEd operates 12 nuclear power units in Illinois, with a total capacity of 11,487 MW, or about 51 percent of the company's overall generating capacity.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
